minutes.headline: Committee authorized busing as many families inside 1.5 miles as possible and a sidewalk ARPA letter.
minutes.summary: Special meeting a week before school opened, dominated by parent objections to ending exceptions to the 1.5-mile bus policy and to unsafe walking routes. The committee voted to have the chair write the select board about ARPA funds for sidewalks, and to authorize the superintendent to accommodate as many bus requests as possible in consultation with counsel. Policy review, a transportation coordinator and extra buses were left for later.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted 5-0 to authorize the superintendent to bus as many families as possible inside the 1.5-mile line, in consultation with counsel.
The committee voted 5-0 to have the chair write the select board, and state legislators, about using ARPA funds for sidewalks.
Parents raised unsafe walking routes, including Mass Ave and Northfield Road, and inconsistent application of the busing policy, in public comment a week before school opened.
A member asked whether ESSER funds could pay for a one-year transportation coordinator; the business manager is to review eligibility and report back if the committee wishes.
Policy review, the drop-off age policy and parent communication were set for future agendas; adding a bus was noted as needing a funding source.

why_it_matters: The vote widens bus access for families inside 1.5 miles for now, but it does not change the written policy, so eligibility could change again once the policy review happens.

Any added bus or coordinator position has to be paid from a budget line or from one-time grant money, so it bears on the school transportation budget and on what the select board does with ARPA money, which it controls.
